status: AI design study; unscored raster concept, not a font or foundry product

sources.basis: Primary source and observations supplied by parent in foundry-sources.json; no claim of independent page inspection in this subtask.
sources.reference_observation: Lava is described for magazine/text use at small and large sizes; Greek and Latin credited to Peter Bilak.
sources.creative_inference: Native-script integrity, warm rhythm, open counters and robust small forms are proposed exploration goals, not a claim to copy Lava outlines or represent all Typotheque work.

useful_glyph_ideas: Large italic theta: broad oval, generous interior light, level crossing and stronger outer stroke; deliberately reconstruct and balance both counter spaces.
Large italic beta: tall curved spine with unequal bowls and a narrow open transition; explore the lower bowl width without congesting the join.
Large italic xi: three clearly staged motions with a small upper flick and broad lower returning curve; consider as a rhythm proposal rather than tracing it.
Large italic alpha: asymmetric open-looking counter relationship, firm rising right stroke and economical exit; retain Greek identity while testing text rhythm.
Upsilon has a spacious cupped body while nu has a sharper asymmetric trough; this is a useful construction hypothesis for separating the Greek pair.
Bold rows suggest retaining broad theta/omicron spaces and open Greek flow as weight grows; exact family compatibility still requires vector work.
visible_errors_and_limitations: Critical contrast failure: the enlarged glyph labelled Latin v has a rounded, returning Greek-like construction instead of the requested angular Latin wedge. Do not adopt it as Latin v or treat the trio as a solved distinction.
Upright and italic full alphabets, final sigma and variant rows appear present on visual inspection; raster appearance cannot establish Unicode coverage or exact variant mappings.
Script kappa resembles a cursive x and alternate rho has a q-like return; semantic recognizability and distinction from Latin x/q require scrutiny at actual size.

The two displayed equations appear mathematically correct on inspection: diffusion equation and normalized Gaussian density. This does not certify a working math font, MATH table, shaping or formula layout.

Text/Script/Script-script examples are labelled 12/10/8 pt inside an image. These labels are not calibrated physical sizes and do not demonstrate a true optical-size system; the small rows may largely be scaled forms.

The image emphasizes open curves but much of the full alphabet remains conservative and close to familiar Greek math conventions. It is a selective anatomy direction rather than proof of a wholly new coherent family.
Actual resolution is below the requested target, so contour decisions, fine terminal behavior and small-size reliability cannot be read as precise geometry.
No foundry authorship, expert endorsement, council score, vector quality or production readiness is implied.
